profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a university-affiliated hospital research unit preparing the next handoff between the qualitative analysis team and the clinical recruitment/site-liaison workstream for a narrative inquiry study on changing multidisciplinary team power dynamics during COVID-19 in Irish healthcare settings. The immediate context is that the principal investigator wants a single integrated progress pack by Friday for an advisory-group review, and the two attendees need to align on what materials will be shared, how interview waves are labeled, what counts as a 'site summary,' and who updates the shared participant tracking sheet. The agenda is to review current interview coverage, confirm the status of the latest summaries, align the handoff from data collection to analysis, and clarify what will be placed in the shared folder for the Friday review. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the handoff package, timeline, and ownership of routine updates, even though subtle assumption gaps remain.

members.name: Dr. Aoife Brennan
members.expertise: Narrative inquiry, thematic analysis, interview coding, reflexive memoing
members.background: Aoife is a postdoctoral researcher in health services research who joined the project after the interview protocol was finalized and now leads the analysis workstream for the COVID-era MDT narratives.
members.private_state: She wants a clean, analysis-ready packet for the advisory group without reopening methodological debates, and she is worried that inconsistent site documentation will make the emerging cross-site comparisons look weaker than they are.
hidden_assumptions: A 'site summary' is an analytic briefing note synthesizing patterns across all interviews completed for one hospital site, not a running operational log.
The 'wave 2 interviews' label refers to the second analytic batch prepared after transcript cleaning, regardless of when participants were actually interviewed.
A participant being 'ready' means the transcript has been checked, pseudonymized, and can be circulated internally for coding.
The shared tracker is owned by the recruitment/site-liaison side for participant-level status, while analysis only adds coding-stage notes in the memo column.

members.name: Siobhan Kelly
members.expertise: Site coordination, participant scheduling, ethics-compliant data handling, hospital liaison
members.background: Siobhan is an experienced coordinator who managed recruitment and interview logistics across three hospital groups during the pandemic and maintains the study's operational records and hospital contacts.
members.private_state: She wants to show the advisory group that fieldwork is under control and evenly covered across professions, and she is concerned that analysis keeps treating operational documents as if they were final outputs before all late interviews are in.
hidden_assumptions: A 'site summary' is a concise operational snapshot listing which professions have been interviewed at that site, who is still pending, and notable access constraints.
The 'wave 2 interviews' label refers to the second chronological round of interviews conducted after the winter surge period.
A participant being 'ready' means consent, recording, and secure filing are complete, even if transcript checking and pseudonymization are still pending.
Once analysis starts using the shared tracker for Friday reporting, the analysis side will update current statuses directly rather than sending edits back through coordination.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to include a 'site summary' for each hospital in the Friday pack.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a short analytic synthesis of narrative patterns about hierarchy, autonomy, and meeting structure across interviews from each site.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a logistical snapshot showing recruitment coverage by profession, pending participants, and contextual access notes for each site.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both workstreams already use the same phrase internally, and in a coordination meeting it sounds natural to say the summaries are 'almost done' without specifying whether they are analytic or operational documents.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss folding the 'wave 2 interviews' into the handoff and Friday review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the second prepared transcript batch, which includes some earlier-conducted interviews that only recently cleared transcription and cleaning.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to interviews conducted in the later pandemic period after the winter surge, regardless of whether the transcripts are processed yet.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The project has both a fieldwork timeline and an analysis batching rhythm, and both are commonly described as 'waves'; because the counts roughly overlap, each hears the phrase as straightforward.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a participant being 'ready'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having the remaining participants 'ready' before the pack is finalized.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'ready' means transcript checked, de-identified, and usable in internal analytic summaries.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'ready' means interview completed with consent and files stored correctly, even if processing steps are not finished.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In mixed research operations, 'ready' is a routine shorthand for being sufficiently advanced for the next handoff, and each assumes the other's threshold is the standard one for their own stage.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the shared tracker will be kept current ahead of Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes M2 will continue to maintain participant statuses and that analysis will only add memo links or note analytic progress when necessary.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes M1 will directly revise statuses for anything analysis is now using in the Friday pack, so the tracker becomes a jointly edited live document.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see themselves as being collaborative rather than territorial, so saying the tracker will be 'kept current' feels sufficient; ownership norms are second-order workflow habits that are rarely verbalized unless something breaks.

turns.inner_thought: If we can get one clean pack together by Friday, I can avoid another circular discussion about methods and keep the advisory group focused on the narrative patterns. I need the site summary for each hospital group to mean an analytic synthesis, and I want the wave 2 interviews folded in as the second prepared transcript batch so the cross-site comparisons look mature rather than patchy.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. I thought it would be useful just to get the Friday pack aligned across recruitment and analysis, make sure the site summary for each hospital is going in, and fold the wave 2 interviews into the handoff and the Friday review.

turns.inner_thought: Good, this should help show the advisory group that fieldwork is steady and balanced across sites. From my side, the later COVID-period interviews are the main thing still moving, and if the last scheduled people complete, I can say the remaining participants are ready this week in the operational sense.
turns.utterance: Yes, that makes sense. Coverage is looking fairly solid across the three hospital groups, and the remaining participants should be ready this week, especially the ones from the later COVID period, so I think we can show things are moving in the right direction.

turns.inner_thought: Once those transcripts are checked, pseudonymized, and usable, I can finish the analytic briefs site by site. I really need that final bit of processing done so I can write the summaries cleanly and not hedge too much on the cross-site themes.
turns.utterance: That would help a lot. Once those are ready, I can finish the site summaries for the three hospital groups and make the cross-site patterns much easier for the advisory group to read.

turns.inner_thought: Interesting that she says finish, because mine are nearly there already as concise site snapshots. I have profession coverage, pending people, and access issues all together, so from my point of view the site summaries are basically done apart from a few final status checks.
turns.utterance: That’s good. My site summaries are nearly complete already, because I’ve the main pieces for each site in one place, so it should be straightforward to have those included.

turns.inner_thought: She must be talking about the same summaries at a practical level, which is fine. On the interview side, several transcripts in the second prepared batch are already clean enough to cite, even if some were conducted earlier, so I can bring wave 2 into the Friday material without waiting on everything else.
turns.utterance: Perfect. On the wave 2 interviews, several are already in the second batch from my side, so I’m expecting to reference them in the Friday material.

turns.inner_thought: That’s reassuring, because the later round still feels just shy of balanced coverage. I’m still looking for one consultant and one physiotherapist from the winter-surge cohort before I’d call wave 2 properly rounded out across professions.
turns.utterance: That’s helpful, because wave 2 still needs one consultant and one physiotherapist before the coverage feels complete, so it’s good that some of that material is already coming through.

turns.inner_thought: I should flag the timing without reopening process debates. What I actually need is not just that the interviews happened, but that the transcripts are checked and de-identified so I can pull extracts safely and send the pack around internally.
turns.utterance: Yes, and really the main thing for me is having the remaining participants ready in time for extracts and a final check before I circulate the pack internally.

turns.inner_thought: That should be fine. Most of them are either already done or booked, and once consent is in order and the files are securely stored, I count them as ready for the tracker and for reporting upward. Analysis can take it from there.
turns.utterance: They’re either done or scheduled at this point, so I’m not too worried. Once consent and filing are closed out, I’d consider them ready for the tracker and the pack.

turns.inner_thought: Good, then Siobhan will keep the participant-level tracker tidy as usual and I can just pull the current statuses from it. I only want to add analysis notes where needed, not get dragged into maintaining operational records.
turns.utterance: Great, then the shared tracker should stay current ahead of Friday, and I’ll pull from it when I’m finalizing what analysis includes.

turns.inner_thought: Exactly. If analysis is now using it for Friday reporting, Aoife can update the statuses directly as transcripts move along, and I can keep my time on the final hospital contacts instead of doing duplicate updates after every handoff.
turns.utterance: Agreed. If analysis updates the statuses directly as things move along, that should let me focus on chasing the last site contacts rather than doubling back into the sheet.

turns.inner_thought: Fine, we’re aligned enough for Friday. I’ll assume she means the tracker will be current from her side, and I can move ahead with the analytic pack: wave 2 as the cleaned second batch, site summaries for each hospital, and a stable basis for the advisory discussion.
turns.utterance: That sounds good. So we’re aligned on adding the wave 2 material, including site summaries for each hospital, and keeping the tracker current before the advisory review.

turns.inner_thought: Good, that gives me a clear line for the week. I’ll finish the remaining operational pieces so the pack shows site coverage as it stands, and once the last participants are ready and the tracker is updated, advisory should see that fieldwork is under control.
turns.utterance: Yes, exactly. I’ll finish what’s still outstanding this week so the Friday pack reflects where things stand across the sites.
